nodes.description: Without CPE, the C-terminal basic residues left after prohormone convertase cleavage are not removed. Most neuropeptides and peptide hormones are therefore reduced, and processing intermediates carrying C-terminal lysine or arginine, which are undetectable in wild-type tissue, accumulate. Some peptides are only partly reduced because carboxypeptidase D can substitute for CPE in the trans-Golgi network and immature granules, and about a tenth are unaffected. The defect is not confined to one tissue: it affects the hypothalamus, pituitary and pancreatic islets, which is why several endocrine axes fail together.

nodes.description: CPE is needed to make many of the peptides that restrain feeding and raise energy expenditure, among them alpha- and beta-MSH from POMC, cholecystokinin, CART peptides and neurotensin. Their combined deficiency is thought to drive the hyperphagia and obesity. The obesity is not explained by POMC processing alone: mice lacking CPE only in POMC-expressing cells are not obese, so peptides made in other brain or peripheral cells must contribute.

nodes.description: Besides its enzymatic role, CPE (also called neurotrophic factor-alpha1) supports neuron survival. Cpe knockout mice develop degeneration of the hippocampal CA3 pyramidal neurons from four weeks of age, with gliosis, absent long-term potentiation and memory deficits, and a neuron-specific knockout reproduces the learning and memory deficits without obesity or altered glucose metabolism. This is the leading mouse explanation for the intellectual disability, but it has not been examined in patients, and whether it depends on the enzyme activity or the non-enzymatic neurotrophic function is not settled.

evidence.snippet: Taken together, the results of this study demonstrate that specific neuronal CPE knockout leads to central nervous system dysfunction in mice, including learning and memory deficits, hippocampal Sub degeneration and impaired neurogenesis.

nodes.description: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone is made from a precursor that requires CPE for its final processing. In Cpe fat/fat mice hypothalamic GnRH is reduced by roughly two thirds and C-terminally extended intermediates accumulate. Patients have low gonadotropins with low sex steroids. How much of the human hypogonadism this explains is open: in male mice the infertility owes more to abnormal sexual behaviour than to the gonadal axis.

nodes.description: In pancreatic beta cells, CPE trims the basic residues left on the proinsulin cleavage intermediates. Its loss leaves proinsulin and partly processed intermediates in the granule and in the circulation, and in mice the beta cells lack mature insulin granules. Elevated proinsulin has been measured in a patient. In the mouse, beta-cell-specific Cpe deletion alone raises proinsulin without causing obesity or diabetes, so the diabetes of the global defect probably also depends on the obesity and other axes.
